ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the lines $y=-x+b$ and $y=kx$ are represented in the same Cartesian coordinate system. What is the solution set of the inequality $-x+b<kx$ with respect to $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From the graph, it is known that the graphs of the two lines intersect at ($-1$, $-3$), \\
$\because$ $-x+b<kx$, \\
$\therefore$ select the part to the right of the intersection point, \\
thus, for $x>-1$, $-x+b<kx$, \\
so the answer is: $\boxed{x>-1}$

method.method_draft: Extract numerical equations from the graph, then solve algebraically. First describe the image: the line y=kx passes through the origin and intersects the other line at the dashed point (-1,-3). Since y=kx contains (-1,-3), substitute to get -3=k(-1), so k=3. The line y=-x+b also contains (-1,-3), so -3=-(-1)+b=1+b, giving b=-4. From the text, solve the inequality -x+b<kx by substituting b=-4 and k=3: -x-4<3x, so -4<4x, hence x>-1.
